answer_2.quote: For paraphrase plagiarism, we perform an evaluation of LLM-paraphrased documents through the lens of semantic equivalence, consistency, and language quality... • Semantic equivalence → BERTScore... • Consistency → AlignScore... • Language quality → Readability index & CoLAScore... For summary evaluation... • Relevance → BLANC... • Coherence → BARTScore...

answer_3.quote: we evaluate Five LLMs... for binary classification of plagiarism and plagiarism type identification... we experiment with four popular prompting techniques: zero-shot vanilla prompting, zero-shot Chain-of-Thought (CoT) prompting, few-shot vanilla prompting, and few-shot CoT prompting.

answer_4.quote: Human annotation plays a critical role in verifying the accuracy and reliability of automated systems. We use Amazon Mechanical Turk (AMT) to hire human annotators for three separate annotation tasks: non-plagiarism evaluation, paraphrase evaluation, and summary evaluation.
answer_4.guideline: For non-plagiarism: 'evaluate if the provided texts plagiarize the source text'; for paraphrase: 'evaluate the overall quality of the provided texts given the source text'; for summary: 'evaluate the overall quality of the provided texts given the source text'.
